description: The Chicago Clay Co-Op is home to 20 full time ceramic artists. Members have 24/7 access to the space and access to a number of essential tools. Our studio is currently at capacity, but please join the waitlist if you’re interested.

members.name: Michael Bridges
members.statement: Michael Bridges is an artist, designer, and instructor based out of Chicago, IL. His approach to ceramics is often horrific, occasionally humorous and tries to tread the fine line between function and form.

members.name: Jen Fitzgerald
members.statement: My work, characterized by its realism and complexity, aims to push the boundaries of traditional ceramics and functionality.

members.name: Lillie Frances
members.statement: Lillie Frances dabbles in regular-sized pottery, but let’s be honest—she’s best known for going small. Like, one-inch-tall. Her miniature masterpieces include everything from moonshine jugs and teapots to candle holders, colanders, and tiny mugs stamped with cheeky little sayings. Find her (and her very small pots) at potterymouthchicago.com or on Instagram @potterymouthchicago

members.name: Linley M. Erickson
members.statement: Linley M. Erickson is an artist and teacher in Chicago, IL. Her work is inspired by traditional Scadinavian folk art and the minature.

members.name: Cassidy Day
members.statement: Cassidy Day is a graphic designer and artist based in Chicago. She began working in ceramics to explore a tactile medium that challenged her relationship to functionality and aesthetics. Her current works are inspired by bold geometry and the balance of structure and spontaneity.

members.name: Xavier Wynn
members.statement: Xavier is one-half of EMXW—a joint exploration of art and life with his partner, Edwige Massart. He creates hand-built sculptures in ceramics where cute meets disconcerting. When not sculpting clay, he hones his skills as an assistant pencil sharpener and works as an illustrator, graphic designer, ux designer, and creative director.

members.name: Marie Enger
members.statement: A cartoonist and illustrator hyper-focused on creating something that looks uncomfortable, but feels good.

members.name: mangi
members.statement: mangi nurtures a ceramics practice focused on freely creating imperfect vessels to celebrate, care for and curate life and vibrant panels to vividly catalogue the current condition.
